text: ハーバー・シティは試合終盤、2-3で負けている中、90+2分に戦い方を変えました。プレッシャーを強めて、もっと直接的な攻めに切り替え、守備のラインも高く上げました。これでボールを奪いやすくして、すぐに得点のチャンスを作ろうとしましたが、まだシュートや決定機は生まれていません[#1884]。対するシーブルック・タウンはボールをよくキープし、広い攻めで試合をコントロールしています。

trace.output: Brief: Harbour City change approach for fan audience in ja

- Harbour City's pressing increased from 0.6 to 0.78 after the tactical change at 90+2' [#1884].
- Directness of play for Harbour City rose from 0.28 to 0.43 post-change [#1884].
- Line height for Harbour City was raised from 0.62 to 0.74 during the tactical shift [#1884].
- Harbour City’s possession improved from 31.7% before to 40.8% after the change [#1884].
- The score remained 2-3 in favor of Seabrook Town at the moment of the tactical change [#1884].

- Harbour City, trailing 2-3, made a tactical change at 90+2' to press higher (press increased from 0.6 to 0.78) and play more direct (directness from 0.28 to 0.43), pushing their defensive line higher (line height from 0.62 to 0.74) in an attempt to quickly regain possession and create scoring chances late in the match [#1884].
- This shift reflects a move away from their usual patient short-passing style paired with a 4-2-3-1 formation towards a more aggressive pressing trap combined with direct forward play, aiming to overload the opponent quickly and reduce build-up times.
- Seabrook Town, set up in a 3-4-3 with wide crossing play, maintained higher possession (56%) and field tilt (61.9%) in the last 10 minutes, indicating they were still controlling the game despite Harbour City's increased press.
- Harbour City's increased pressing likely intended to disrupt Seabrook's wide play and crossing patterns by forcing turnovers higher up the pitch, but with no shots or xG generated after the change, the late tactical shift did not result in an immediate scoring chance.
